chunks.text:
Circulation & email compliance

This is an internal product brief for Ozer Commercial property. It is not legal advice. Agencies should have UK privacy counsel review soft opt-in copy and their own privacy notices.

What “circulation” is

1. Occupiers / investors register a requirement (website embed or CRM).
2. Agents match a disposal to active requirements.
3. Agents circulate particulars by email to that matching set.
4. Recipients can unsubscribe from matching-opportunity emails for that agency.

Email classification

| Message | Class | Pipe |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| “Thanks — we received your requirement” | Transactional / service | ZeptoMail |
| One-to-one reply about a specific enquiry / listing | Transactional / service | ZeptoMail |
| “New letting that may match your registered requirement” (list) | Marketing (solicited / soft opt-in or LI) | Amazon SES |

5. Let or Sold — completed outcome

Workspace subscription

Goal

Choose and manage the Ozer Business plan (and add-ons) that funds this team workspace.

Prerequisites

- Business team account
- Permission to view billing (Settings → Billing)
- Payment method ready for checkout (Stripe)

This is not client invoicing. Client bills live under Client invoices.

Business plans (summary)

Exact prices can change — confirm on ozer.so/pricing. Typical Business products:

| Plan | Best for | Typical inclusions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free (Business Lite) | Apps-only / light use | Marketplace access; pay for apps you use |
| Starter | Solo freelancers | Clients, jobs, invoices; £14 seat 1, then £9 each extra seat |
| Pro | Studios | Everything in Starter, shared AI, 3 guests per seat; £29 seat 1, then £22 each extra seat |

Trials (where offered) are commonly 14 days on paid Business plans. Annual billing on Pro is 10× monthly (16.7% less than 12×).

Delivery lives in Projects (jobs) with phases and tasks, plus Tasks and Planner for day-to-day execution.

Goal

- Projects / Tasks modules enabled under the Work sidebar section

| Tasks | /app/[account]/tasks | Cross-project task inbox |

2. Break it into phases and tasks.

Projects

Goal

Create and run delivery projects linked to clients, with phases and optional client-portal visibility.

Prerequisites

- Business workspace
- Sidebar Work → Projects (/app/[account]/projects)
- Ideally an existing client

Steps: create a project

1. Open Projects in the sidebar.
2. Choose create / new project.
3. Set the project name and link a client.
4. Choose status / dates if prompted.
5. Save. You’ll open the project detail at /app/[account]/projects/[id].

Steps: structure delivery

1. On the project detail page, add phases (milestones or workstreams).
2. Open a phase (/app/[account]/projects/[id]/phases/[phaseId]) to manage its tasks.
3. Assign owners and due dates so Planner and Tasks stay useful.
4. Use edit at /app/[account]/projects/[id]/edit when you need to change basics (client, title, status).

chunks.text:
Security & trust

Ozer is built for studios that care where data lives and who can see it.

Goal

Understand how access works in a Business workspace, what you control as an admin, and where to read formal trust / legal documents.

Prerequisites

- Access to a Business workspace (owner/admin for settings that affect the whole team)

At a glance

- Marketing trust centre: ozer.so/trust
- Workspace data access is enforced with Postgres row-level security (RLS) — the app client only sees rows your membership allows
- Auth uses Supabase Auth; workspace billing uses Stripe
- Desktop activity and email connects add optional data flows — configure them deliberately

Legal: Privacy · Terms · DPA

Steps: lock down a Business workspace

1. Open Team (/app/[account]/members) and audit members and pending invites.
2. Assign the least-privilege role that still lets people do their jobs.
3. Remove people who left the studio; revoke stale invites.
4.

chunks.text:

3. Check whether the data lives in a different account in the switcher (personal vs Business slug).
4. Contact hello@ozer.so with the workspace slug and approximate time of the issue — don’t share passwords or full card numbers.

Tips

- Prefer Business workspaces for client work you’ll share; keep sensitive personal life data in the personal hub.
- Treat portal and guest links like credentials — don’t post them publicly.
- Admins should rarely use elevated admin/service clients in integrations; stick to normal app access so RLS stays in force.

Troubleshooting

| Problem | What to try |
| --- | --- |
| User sees another studio’s data | They’re likely on the wrong workspace — switch accounts |
| User sees too little | Raise role or enable modules; don’t bypass RLS |
| Ex-employee still has access | Remove from Team; rotate shared passwords for any connected email/DNS |
| Compliance questionnaire | Start from Trust and the DPA, then email support for specifics |

chunks.title: Personal & team accounts
chunks.text:
Personal & team accounts

Goal

Choose the right account type for data, sharing, and billing.

Prerequisites

- An Ozer login (Create your account)

Account types

Personal account

- Linked to your user ID (auth.users.id matches accounts.id in Makerkit terms).
- Good for private pipelines, personal projects, planner, and life context that isn’t shared with a studio.
- Reach it via /app and the personal entries in the account switcher.

Team (Business) account

- A shared workspace with members, roles, and shared CRM / projects / invoices.
- Data is scoped by account_id. You only see what your membership allows.
- URLs use the workspace slug: /app/[account]/….
- Billing for Business plans lives under Settings → Billing on that account.

Steps: create another Business workspace

1. Open the account switcher in the sidebar.
2. Create a new team / Business workspace.
3. Name it, set the slug, and pick the Business profile.
4. Invite people from Team (/app/[account]/members) as needed.
